paths.description: Anonymous homepage and login journey, the primary account-entry flow; checked at desktop, mobile, dark, reduced-motion and forced-colors conditions.
Public video showcase representing media discovery and listing templates.
Public groups directory representing community discovery and subscription actions.
Public recommendations page representing content cards, images, topic navigation, and the anonymous acquisition prompt.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the screenshot remains a light surface; computed html color-scheme is light and background remains rgb(235,237,240).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces and controls from prefers-color-scheme, using light-dark() or equivalent tokens.

findings.summary: The cookie banner obscures the primary task on load
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show the fixed cookie banner covering the OK logo and “Log in to OK” heading; on mobile it occupies much of the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface, preserve the primary heading/action, and make it easy to dismiss.

findings.summary: Consent presents an easy accept path but no equally direct reject path
findings.evidence: The first-load banner exposes “Allow all” and “Configure”; there is no equally prominent reject-all control in the captured state.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer accept and reject choices with equal prominence and keep granular configuration secondary, without nagging.

findings.summary: Critical login text fails contrast and mobile zoom is disabled
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 2.66:1 contrast for white “Sign in” text on #ff7700 plus other failures, and the viewport contains maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the orange or change foreground color to meet 4.5:1, fix secondary text contrast, and remove user-scalable=no/maximum-scale=1.

findings.summary: Document structure and accessible semantics are incomplete
findings.evidence: All four representative pages expose no H1; the probe found 16 empty links, and Lighthouse found a presentation-role conflict on the logo.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each template one descriptive H1, remove or name empty links, and correct conflicting presentational/ARIA semantics.

findings.summary: The anonymous entry page is slow and script-heavy
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 7.5s, FCP 6.7s, TBT 330ms and performance 0.49; the trace corroborated a 2.66s LCP in a lighter desktop run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the login shell and LCP resource, defer nonessential work, split long tasks, and load analytics/ads after the primary UI.

findings.summary: Hundreds of scripts and substantial unused code ship before login
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 424 requests, including 297 scripts and 4.64MB transferred script bytes; Lighthouse estimated 1,752KiB unused JavaScript and 556KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split the anonymous shell, conditionally load video/design-system/ad bundles, remove duplicate and legacy code, and defer noncritical CSS.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security policy is weakened
findings.evidence: Headers include CSP but permit unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval with broad sources/connect-src *, while Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval, restrict connect/script/object sources, and add explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Tracking and cookie scope are disproportionate on the anonymous login page
findings.evidence: The page contacted 25 third-party origins and three known trackers; 14 cookies were found, several without Secure, all SameSite=None, and multiple analytics cookies last 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Load optional trackers only after valid consent, reduce vendors and retention, mark every HTTPS cookie Secure, and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential.

findings.summary: Runtime and browser-platform hygiene has regressions
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured an uncaught MobX error, a deprecated unload listener, six BFCache failure reasons, cookie inspector issues, and a best-practices score of 0.54.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the MobX exception, replace unload with pagehide/visibilitychange, and remove actionable BFCache blockers and deprecated APIs.

findings.summary: Public recommendations are effectively absent without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 6% raw/rendered content overlap and classified /discovery as a JS shell; crawler screenshots omit the recommendation content. /video also canonicalises to the homepage and /sitemap.xml returned 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful listing content and per-route title/canonical data, preserve crawlable hrefs, and publish sitemap entries for public templates.

findings.summary: Language metadata does not match localized content
findings.evidence: The groups page declares html lang=en while its title and substantial visible group content are Russian; this gives assistive technology and translation tools the wrong language signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Set the document language to the active locale and mark isolated mixed-language strings with lang attributes; keep direction metadata locale-aware.

findings.summary: The login form gives no blank-submit recovery and omits autofill tokens
findings.evidence: Clicking submit with empty fields produced no visible validation/error state and no :invalid controls; email and password inputs have no autocomplete values.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints, validate after interaction, announce actionable errors, and add username/current-password autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Resource and image delivery is wasteful for the public shell
findings.evidence: The page transfers 6.37MB and 98.5% of bytes are from third-party origins. Discovery has 23/24 images without dimensions, four oversized images, five legacy-format images, and four missing responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set image dimensions, serve AVIF/WebP responsive sources, lazy-load below-fold cards, and enforce route-specific third-party and byte budgets.

findings.summary: The login page has an unusually large in-memory footprint
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary reports 1,105,205 nodes and 74,077,369 self-size bytes for a simple anonymous login surface. A second independent load was similar, indicating a consistently large footprint.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid initialising media, editor and large design-system modules on login; lazy-load route-only modules and profile DOM/closure populations after each reduction.

findings.summary: Route changes do not provide continuity
findings.evidence: Representative public navigation uses ordinary page links, and no transition treatment was observed in the route captures; content swaps are abrupt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin public routes and respect reduced motion.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is custom rather than a semantic overlay primitive
findings.evidence: The rendered probe found zero dialog, popover, and details elements while a modal-like consent layer blocks content at the top of every captured page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an appropriately labelled dialog for consent, with focus management, Escape/cancel behavior, and a non-modal compact presentation where possible.

findings.summary: Several controls have undersized hit areas
findings.evidence: The rendered probe found 17 visible interactive targets below 24px in at least one dimension, including the 18px-high account-recovery control and multiple 16px-high navigation links.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand interactive hit areas toward at least 44 CSS px without changing visual density and retain visible keyboard focus.

findings.summary: Non-content chrome crowds public content
findings.evidence: On groups and videos, a top consent bar, left navigation and ads, and a fixed bottom login acquisition bar consume substantial viewport space around the primary cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse nonessential acquisition chrome, reserve one clear prompt, and prioritise the content grid in the available viewport.

findings.summary: Password remains the primary sign-in path without a visible passkey option
findings.evidence: The login surface offers password and federated providers but no visible passkey/WebAuthn route; the password inputs also lack autocomplete metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in/conditional UI with password and federated methods as fallbacks, and advertise it in account security settings.
